title: I spent $50 on AI tools and shipped my first game in 3 weeks.
author: InkFusionNova
selftext:
Hi everyone!

I wanted to share my story. Maybe it’ll inspire someone to take their first step, just like other developers’ stories once inspired me.

I’m 30 years old, and I’ve dreamed of making video games ever since I was a teenager. But life had other plans: work, moving between countries, war, immigration… There was always a reason to tell myself, “I’ll do it later.”

A few months ago, I decided I didn’t want to wait for the “perfect moment” anymore.

I actually started working on two dream game projects at the same time. Very quickly, though, I realized they were far too ambitious for my first real release. I estimated each one would take at least six months, probably more.

To be honest, I started losing motivation. Every day I was making progress, but the finish line still felt incredibly far away. I was afraid I’d burn out and end up shelving my dream once again.

So I changed my approach.

Instead of trying to build my dream game first, I decided to create something I could actually finish. I wanted to prove to myself that I was capable of taking a project all the way to release. I knew that confidence would help me keep moving toward my bigger goals.

That’s when I decided to build a modern take on the classic Snake.

Before I started, I spent some time exploring Google Play and noticed that most Snake games felt almost identical. My goal became keeping the spirit of the original while adding much more variety and replayability.

The final game includes:

\* 34 campaign levels

\* Classic mode

\* Survival mode

\* Dream Mode with a large open map

\* A custom room editor

\* Snake customization

\* Achievements

\* Google Play Games integration

\* Cloud saves

\* Support for 15 languages

The very first prototype took just one day.

But that’s when the real work began.

Most of my time wasn’t spent on gameplay at all. It went into Google Play Games integration, cloud saves, localization, performance optimization, publishing to Google Play, and fighting an endless stream of bugs.

I’m sure many developers know that feeling: fix one issue… and two more immediately appear.

AI became a huge part of my workflow.

ChatGPT acted as the project’s architect, helping me think through technical decisions and overall architecture.

I used Codex and Claude as coding agents, assigning them individual development tasks and reviewing their work.

Whenever I hit usage limits, I switched to Grok for smaller tasks.

If I only count the cost of AI tools, the entire project cost me around $50.

From start to release, the game took about three weeks.

Yes, it’s “just” a small mobile game.

But to me, it means much more than that.

It’s the first game I’ve ever taken all the way to release.

More importantly, it proved to me that the dream I’d been putting off for years is still possible.

I’m now back to working on those two larger projects that I originally paused—but this time with a completely different mindset. I know I can finish what I start.

Neon Snake wasn’t my final goal.

It was my first real step toward becoming a game developer.

If you’re curious to see what three weeks of AI-assisted game development looks like, the game is already available on Google Play under the name Neon Snake: Dream Mode.

I’d genuinely love to hear your thoughts. Whether it’s praise, criticism, or suggestions for improvement, all feedback is welcome.

Thanks for reading! 

**P.S.** If life feels overwhelming right now, don’t worry about taking giant steps. Just take the next small one. Start with something you know you can finish. It doesn’t have to be perfect or ambitious—it just has to move you forward. Sometimes one small achievement is enough to restore your confidence, reignite your motivation, and remind you that you’re capable of much more than you think.
